text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Social Affairs Minister Ad Melkert opposes increase in
social security premiums after recent disclosure of multi-
billion-guilder shortfall in social security funds. (p1)
- Dutch investors welcome British investor's attempt to
force Shell oil group to include references
to environment and human rights in its annual report. (p1)
- Germany's Bundespost drops courier service TNT following
its acquisition by Dutch PTT Post. (p1)
- Industrial group Stork's Fokker Aviation unit
fears for future if bid to relaunch Fokker succeeds. (p3)
- Dutch business confidence rises further in January. (p1)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Despite talk of public debate to settle the issue, Dutch
government has already decided that Amsterdam's Schiphol
airport must be allowed to expand. (p1)
- Insurance industry watchdog Verzekeringskamer and the
government are responsible for damages arising from
collapse of insurer Vie d'Or several years ago, Groningen
university professors conclude. (p2)
- Shopkeepers may pass on costs of using new electronic
payment cards to consumers, EU Commission says. (p2)
- ABN AMRO Bank still has 10.1 pct stake in Content
after having to buy temporary employment agency's
shares last year in price support operation. (p15) DE TELEGRAAF
- Prices of car parts may increase by up to 100 percent as a
result of new European ruling. (p1)
- Unions demand strong increase in social security premiums
in order to bridge recent shortfall in social funds. (p3)
- Real estate fund Rodamco expects to finalise
talks about takeover of Imry property portfolio from
Barclays Bank. (p23) TROUW
- Liberal party (VVD) leader Frits Bolkestein wants cabinet
to present plans for expansion of Schiphol airport before
next year's election. (p1)
- Investment company Begemann no longer involved in
plan to relaunch bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Builder HBG wins orders worth 220 million guilders as
part of project to build traffic intersection in
U.S. city of Boston. (p10)
